newsitem.title: GERMANY: Bonn gold plan better than loose EMU - Schaeuble.
newsitem.headline: Bonn gold plan better than loose EMU - Schaeuble.

text.p: A senior German government figure said on Thursday that Bonn's plan to revalue central bank gold and reserves was a better option than heading for a loose interpretation of European monetary union (EMU) entry criteria.

Wolfgang Schaeuble, parliamentary leader of Chancellor Helmut Kohl's Christian Democrats (CDU), said in an interview with Reuters that the Bonn coalition believed that allowing a loose EMU interpretation was "the worse alternative" available.

Schaeuble added that the government had not however counted on the Bundesbank being so forthright in its opposition to the revaluation plan and said it would ensure that the current diference of views "did not escalate".
"The room for manoeuvre on discussions are limited in 1997," Schaeuble nonetheless added when asked if he saw any scope for a compromise between Bonn and the central bank.

The government's decision to proceed with a revaluation of Bundesbank gold and currency reserves up towards market prices "underlined (Bonn's) determination to introduce the euro on time and without a relaxation of the criteria," he added.
Schaeuble said that the government's plan to overrule Bundesbank opposition to the revaluation meant in no way that the Bundesbank's independence on monetary policy was reduced.
Finance Minister Theo Waigel said earlier that he believed that Germany could qualify for EMU with or without the revaluation.
